questions.problem:
For the matrix
$C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 7 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}].$
find the minor ${M}_{12}$ of the entry ${c}_{12}.$

${M}_{12}=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The minor of ${c}_{12}=2$ (first row, second column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $2$ are removed: 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 2 & ∗ \\ 0 & ∗ & 4 \\ 7 & ∗ & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${c}_{12}=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{12} & =\text{det}[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot 6-4\cdot 7 \\  & =0-28 \\  & =-28.\end{aligned}
$$

$B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 4 & 0 & 5 \\ 7 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}].$
find the minor ${M}_{22}$ of the entry ${b}_{22}.$

${M}_{22}=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The minor of ${b}_{22}=0$ (second row, second column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $0$ are removed: 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & ∗ & -3 \\ ∗ & 0 & ∗ \\ 7 & ∗ & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${b}_{22}=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{22} & =\text{det}[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot 6-(-3)\cdot 7 \\  & =6-(-21) \\  & =6+21 \\  & =27.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
What is the minor of ${t}_{33}$ in the matrix
$T=[\begin{aligned}y-x & x & {y}^{2} \\ -x & y+x & 1 \\ {x}^{2} & {y}^{2} & {x}^{2}\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the third row and third column:

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}y-x & x & ∗ \\ -x & y+x & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & {x}^{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

Next, we calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}y-x & x \\ -x & y+x\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}y-x & x \\ -x & y+x\end{aligned}| \\  & =(y-x)\cdot (y+x)-x\cdot (-x) \\  & ={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}+{x}^{2} \\  & ={y}^{2}-\cancel{{x}^{2}}+\cancel{{x}^{2}} \\  & ={y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we remove the third row and second column:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}3s & ∗ & 2t \\ -r & ∗ & r \\ ∗ & 4r & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}3s & 2t \\ -r & r\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}3s & 2t \\ -r & r\end{aligned}| \\  & =3s\cdot r-2t\cdot (-r) \\  & =3rs-(-2rt) \\  & =3rs+2rt\end{aligned}

$M=[\begin{aligned}-50 & g & f \\ f & {g}^{2} & {f}^{2} \\ 20g & g & -5\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the third row and first column:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}∗ & g & f \\ ∗ & {g}^{2} & {f}^{2} \\ 20g & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

Next, we calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}g & f \\ {g}^{2} & {f}^{2}\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}g & f \\ {g}^{2} & {f}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =g\cdot {f}^{2}-f\cdot {g}^{2} \\  & =g{f}^{2}-f{g}^{2} \\  & =gf(f-g)\end{aligned}

$$

$x=$

questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate the minor of ${c}_{32},$ we remove the third row and second column: 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}x & ∗ & 3 \\ 4 & ∗ & 6 \\ ∗ & 8 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${c}_{32}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}x & 3 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}x & 3 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =x\cdot 6-3\cdot 4 \\  & =6x-12.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-12 & =18 \\ 6x & =30 \\ x & =5.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Given that the minor of ${d}_{31}$ is $43$, find all the possible values of $x$ in the matrix

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 & -5 \\ 9 & 11 & x \\ 7 & -5 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the third row and first column:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 1 & -5 \\ ∗ & 11 & x \\ 7 & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${d}_{31}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ 11 & x\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ 11 & x\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot x-11\cdot (-5) \\  & =x+55.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${d}_{31}$ is $43$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+55 & =43 \\ x & =-12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-12.$

$$

$$

questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate the minor of ${a}_{11},$ we remove the first row and first column:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & p & 7 \\ ∗ & -8 & p-15\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${a}_{11}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}p & 7 \\ -8 & p-15\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}p & 7 \\ -8 & p-15\end{aligned}| \\  & =p(p-15)-7(-8) \\  & ={p}^{2}-15p+56.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the minor of ${m}_{22}$ is $3{k}^{2}-45$, find all the possible values of $k$ in the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 1 \\ 3 & -4 & -1 \\ 9k-15 & 9 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and second column:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & ∗ & 1 \\ ∗ & -4 & ∗ \\ 9k-15 & ∗ & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${m}_{22}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 9k-15 & -3\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 9k-15 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-3)-(9k-15)\cdot 1 \\  & =-6-(9k-15) \\  & =-9k+9.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${m}_{22}$ is $3{k}^{2}-45$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}-9k+9 & =3{k}^{2}-45 \\ -3k+3 & ={k}^{2}-15 \\ {k}^{2}+3k-18 & =0 \\ (k-3)(k+6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $k=3$ and $k=-6.$

Calculate the minor of the entry $b_{21}$ in the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}10 & 1 & 5 \\ 3 & 6 & 8 \\ 4 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The minor of $b_{21} = 3$ (second row, first column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $3$ are removed: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}∗ & 1 & 5 \\ 3 & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of $b_{21}=3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot 2-5\cdot 7 \\  & =2-35 \\  & =-33.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
[\begin{aligned}7x & 0 & -3y \\ 1 & x+2y & 4 \\ -y & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and second column: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}7x & ∗ & -3y \\ ∗ & x+2y & ∗ \\ -y & ∗ & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Next, we calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}7x & -3y \\ -y & 5\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}7x & -3y \\ -y & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =7x\cdot 5-(-3y)\cdot (-y) \\  & =35x-3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ find all the possible values of $k$ in the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 3 & -1 \\ -5 & 2 & 7 \\ -1 & 2k & -6\end{aligned}]
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and third column:

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 3 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & 7 \\ -1 & 2k & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of $a_{23}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot 2k-3\cdot (-1) \\  & =2{k}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{k}^{2}+3 & =5 \\ 2{k}^{2} & =2 \\ {k}^{2} & =1 \\ k & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $k=-1$ and $k=1.$
